audit_result.proof_trace: Every `cancel()` implementation (LegionAbstractSale L603, LegionSealedBidAuctionSale L199, LegionPreLiquidOpenApplicationSale L226, LegionPreLiquidApprovedSale L483) carries `whenNotPaused`, causing it to revert with EnforcedPause when the sale is paused. The property asserts cancel must succeed while paused, but the proof breaks immediately at this modifier — there is no override removing it. This creates an operational deadlock: if Legion pauses for a security reason, the project owner cannot cancel without Legion first unpausing, temporarily re-opening the attack surface.
audit_result.attack_scenario: Legion pauses a sale mid-flight due to a detected exploit; the project owner calls `cancel()` to unwind investor positions, but `whenNotPaused` reverts the call. Legion must unpause (re-exposing the vulnerability window) before the project can cancel, potentially allowing the exploit to proceed during that gap.
